subject: NUMVAL-C function
notes: NOT-IMPLEMENTED -> CONFORMS, re-verdicted by the kb/Work PB245 golden round (2026-09-09). THE RULE: §15.68.3 r7, NUMVAL-C's twin of §15.67.3 r4 - 35 under standard-binary, 34 under standard-decimal (cite.py --check 15.68.3 'If standard-decimal arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 34' -> OK, rule 7). The standard-binary sentence is unreachable by kb/Work PB198's documented §4.2.6 decline of the mode (see AR-15.67.3-4). DERIVED BEFORE THE RUN, and the derivation turns on a word: what r7 bounds is the DIGIT count, and the currency string is not a digit (§15.68.4 r2 - 'The currency string, if any, and any grouping separators preceding the decimal separator are ignored'), so '$' + 25 + 9 digits is a 34-digit argument-1 AT the bound and required to be accepted, while one more fraction digit is 35 and yields §15.3's implementor default 0 with checking off. MEASURED: exactly that pair. ⛔ THE PAIR HAD TO BE WRITTEN ON NUMVAL-C ITSELF: pb60_numval_standard_decimal measures this boundary on NUMVAL, and a sibling's control is not a witness for this rule - the same reason l1_numval_family_cap_discriminators had to exist beside pb33 for the NATIVE half. WHAT CLOSED IT: PB33/PB34 plus the DigitCapFlag/NumvalDigitCap single table; the row's 'threaded to the TestNumval arms and to nothing else' note is stale. || editions 2014,2023 (kb/Work PB3173, S0b; DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §6 step 0): conditioned on standard-binary or standard-decimal arithmetic, both 2014 introductions.
